Multiple domestic roll formers and steel processors partnered with the PV sector in 2024, supported by a robust U.S. steel industry with only about 13% net import reliance (USGS 2025). While welded steel tube imports serve a wide range of industrial applications, only a small fraction can be attributed to PV. Based on these factors, we estimate that more than 75% of torque tubes deployed in the U.S. PV industry are domestically manufactured. Appendix B provides detailed analysis and assumptions. Torque tubes used in PV tracker systems are probably classified under multiple HTS codes depending on their material, shape, and manufacturing process (see Appendix C). Between 2015 and 2024, the United States imported $0.5–$1.2 billion of welded steel tubes every year; Canada and Mexico together consistently accounted for more than half of total import value each year. Because U.S. welded steel tube imports serve a wide range of non-solar industrial applications, we cannot determine from the trade data whether these trends are consistent with PV torque tube imports. In 2024, estimated PV torque tube demand was around 930,000 t of steel (Appendix B), while U.S. welded tube imports totaled roughly $889 million, equivalent to about 680,000 t.44 Given that PV torque tube demand in 2024 alone exceeded all welded tube imports serving multiple industries, and the U.S. steel sector meets more than 75% of national consumption from domestic sources, it is reasonable to conclude that most torque tubes are manufactured domestically. 44 U.S. International Trade Commission trade data for welded tube (2024): customs value ~$889.1 million, first unit quantity 680.36 million kg (~680,000 t), roughly translating to $1.3/kg ($1,300/t) of import custom value. 76 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Imports from USMCA partners such as Canada and Mexico are duty-free. Base import duties from other countries—such as Taiwan, South Korea, and India—with Most Favored Nation status are also zero for the relevant HTS codes. However, they may still be subject to additional tariffs, such as Section 232 steel tariffs, or AD/CVD measures depending on product type and country of origin. 4.3.4 Regional Pricing for Torque Tubes The domestically manufactured torque tube cost in 2024 was about $0.05/W when used in a dc 100-MW single-axis tracking system. This assumes manufacturers pass through roughly half of dc the 45X MPTC to buyers,45 equivalent to a reduction of about $0.01/W (U.S. Department of dc Energy 2024d). Data from industry interviews suggested that domestically produced torque tube prices were about 30% higher than the prices of imported counterparts in 2024; however, domestically produced torque tubes are cost-competitive because they can help PV projects receive an ITC domestic content bonus. Globally, the price of torque tubes can be as low as $0.025/W in certain regions, particularly in dc markets with lower raw material, fabrication, galvanizing, and manufacturing expenses driven by lower labor or overhead costs (Business Analytiq 2025).
